one_line_contribution: When a reflective prompt optimizer (GEPA) is trained on exactly the same episodes that built an ExpeL-style procedural-memory bank, most of the memory-vs-no-memory accuracy gap collapses, and a single frozen instruction compiled offline from the bank (no inference-time retrieval) matches per-instance top-k retrieval at matched token budget — implying that a large share of published procedural-memory gains is really 'gain over an un-optimized baseline prompt' rather than evidence that retrieval-at-inference is doing anything a static prompt couldn't.
closest_prior_work: MemDelta (arXiv 2606.29914) is correctly identified by the proposal itself as the nearest work: it also shows agent-memory headline gains are baseline artifacts. It threatens novelty on genus (confounded-baseline framing) but not on species (its confound is inside the retrieval pipeline — embeddings, retrieval engineering — while this proposal's is a rival container for the information, instruction optimization, with a compilation prediction MemDelta never makes). More concerning is the proposal's own disclosure: an earlier draft's Preprint Collision Check cited five specific-looking papers (including 'TERMS-Bench,' described by a prior reviewer as 'a GEPA-based substitution test for an architectural intervention in negotiation agents') that the current search could not verify and had to retract. TERMS-Bench, if it exists as described, is structurally closer to this proposal's central move than MemDelta is — using a prompt optimizer as the control for a non-prompt intervention is exactly this paper's methodological trick, just in a different domain. The authors admit they cannot rule this out.
strongest_objection: Every quantitative claim (S ≥ 0.6 on E1, ≥ 0.7 on E2, the compiled-arm-within-2-points prediction) is carried by a single load-bearing model, Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct. The only cross-model evidence is an '8B moderation check' restricted to 4 of the 7 grid cells, 1 decoding seed, n=300 — explicitly a risk-factor spot-check, not a replication of the primary claim. The track brief itself flags that a small model 'may fail to follow a long optimized instruction while still using concrete exemplars,' which is precisely the mechanism that would make S model-size-dependent. If substitution strength scales with instruction-following capacity (plausible and not excluded by this design), the actual finding is 'sufficiently capable models can compile their own memory,' a narrower and much less surprising claim than 'procedural memory is a substitutable container' — and a single 14B data point plus a partial 8B check cannot distinguish the two. This is the classic generality objection that sinks single-model empirical claims at ICLR.
what_would_fix_it: Run the full 7-cell E1 grid (not just the reduced moderation cells) on at least one additional model spanning the 7B–32B range the track specifies, so S can be reported as a function of model capability rather than a single point estimate. Separately, restore a minimal (even 2-cell) version of I2 (optimize-with-memory-in-context) — currently cut entirely — since the track's own motivating brief is titled around 'coupling' and lists co-adaptation as open question 4; without any I2 data the proposal cannot speak to whether jointly-adapted memory+optimizer systems (the actual deployed pattern the track describes) behave differently from the independently-optimized I1 arm this study tests.
missing_baseline: I2 (optimize-with-memory-in-context): the condition where GEPA evolves the instruction while the memory bank is present and retrievable during optimization, i.e. the co-adapted system the track's own abstract describes as the status quo ('agent frameworks now bolt a self-editing memory onto a prompt optimizer'). The proposal explicitly cuts this cell as testing 'co-adaptation, not substitution,' but that means the one deployment configuration practitioners actually use is never measured — the study characterizes independence (I1 built with no memory in context) but says nothing directly about whether joint optimization produces a different, possibly larger or smaller, memory contribution than the isolated-optimizer condition it substitutes for it.
preprint_collision: Substantive and unusually self-critical: it names MemDelta as the closest work and correctly distinguishes genus (confounded baselines) from species (rival-container substitution, compilation prediction), discusses EvoClinician as a near-miss baseline-table precedent, and explicitly reports a residual risk that OpenReview 2026 submissions weren't swept. But the check also discloses that an earlier version fabricated or could not substantiate five specific citations (ActMem, MAS-PromptBench, TERMS-Bench, MemAPO, 'Evaluating Memory Structure in LLM Agents'), one of which — TERMS-Bench — is hedged as possibly real and would be the single closest structural precedent to this paper's core trick if it exists. A search process that has already produced plausible-sounding phantom citations in this same document cannot be fully trusted to have cleared the field on a second pass; the novelty claim should be treated as provisional, not established, until verified against an independent, human-run literature search rather than the proposal's own retry.
